newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris bourse ends lower after Jospin speech.
newsitem.headline: Paris bourse ends lower after Jospin speech.

text.p: French shares finished down but well above their lows on Thursday after Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin outlined his government's programme to parliament.
Some of his comments discouraged investors but the market recovered from its initial slump.
"We already knew most of what he said," a Paris trader said.
The blue chip CAC-40 index finished down 12.05, or 0.44 percent, at 2,739.69 while the CAC-40 June futures fell 18 points to 2,730.
LVMH fell 3.05 percent to 1,461 francs in reaction to the company's buying of shares in Grand Met. Grand Met said late on Thursday that LVMH now owns 6.29 percent of its shares.
Brokers said investors are not happy LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault is buying stock in Grand Met as part of his bid to foil the planned Grand Met-Guinness merger.
"People don't like that cavalier attitude," a broker said. "If he's going to pursue them with legal means, fine, but now he's buying stock."
Moulinex rose 4.20 percent to 149 francs after posting its first profits since 1991 and a rise in productivity.
Dealers said the restructuring by chairman Pierre Blayau appeared to be drawing investors. "The Blayau effect is in full play," said one.
Alcatel Alsthom was unchanged at 652 francs after it announced it expected to double operating profit in 1997.

Thomson-CSF, which at one time was off more than four percent in reaction to Jospin's comments saying the government did not favour privatisations, rose 0.33 percent to close at 152.40 francs after the prime minister said later in his speech that he hopes to boost the French defence sector's competitiveness to pave the way for European alliances.
Lyonnaise des Eaux closed down 1.39 percent at 566 francs after its shareholders gave final approval to the company's merger with Groupe Suez, which closed down 0.77 percent at 295.80 francs.
